in the right diagram — that is, the pushout classifies sharp binary multimaps.

∎

Theorem 7.5
.

Both the
4
-ary multicategories
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}
and
\mathbb{P}\mathbf{sd}^{\sharp}
are left representable and closed, with internal homs
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}
and
\mathbf{Psd}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}
.

Proof.

Since both
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}
and
\mathbb{P}\mathbf{sd}
are left representable, and since
\mathbf{G}\text{-}\mathbf{Cat}
is cocomplete, by Proposition
7.4
both
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}
and
\mathbb{P}\mathbf{sd}^{\sharp}
admit nullary and binary map classifiers. Therefore, by Section
2.5
it remains to show that both are closed. The arguments in both cases are identical in form, and we will give the proof in the case of
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}
.

Let us write
I_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}}\colon\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
for the inclusion. We will prove that the closedness bijections for
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}
on the bottom row below

\textstyle{\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}_{n}(\,\mathcal{A}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{A}_{n};\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}\,)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{I_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}}\circ_{1}-}
\scriptstyle{\lambda_{n+1}^{\sharp}}
\textstyle{\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}_{n+1}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{A}_{n},\mathcal{B};\mathcal{C})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\textstyle{\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{t}_{n}(\,\mathcal{A}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{A}_{n};\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})\,)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\scriptstyle{\lambda_{n+1}}
\textstyle{\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{t}_{n+1}(\mathcal{A}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{A}_{n},\mathcal{B};\mathcal{C})}

restrict to bijections as on the top row — this will imply closedness, since it implies that
\lambda_{n+1}^{\sharp}(F)=\lambda_{n+1}(I_{\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}}\circ F)=(ev\circ_{1}I_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}})\circ F
, and so exhibits
ev\circ_{1}I_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}}\colon\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s},\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}
as witnessing the bijections on the top row.

The case
n=0
is trivial. For
n=1
, consider a tight binary map
\overline{F}\colon\mathcal{A}_{1}\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
. The associated tight binary map
F\colon\mathcal{A}_{1},\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}
will be sharp just when
F^{a_{1}}
and
F_{b}
are strict. Since
F
is tight, this is just to say that each
F^{a_{1}}
is strict — that is, belongs to
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}
— which is to say that
\overline{F}
factors uniquely through
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}
.

For
n=2
, consider a tight binary map
\overline{F}\colon\mathcal{A}_{1},\mathcal{A}_{2}\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
with
F\colon\mathcal{A}_{1},\mathcal{A}_{2},\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}
the associated tight ternary map. To say that
\overline{F}
factors through
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
via a sharp binary map is, since the inclusion is full, equally to say that the unary maps
\overline{F}^{a_{1}}
and
\overline{F}_{a_{2}}
lift to strict maps
\mathcal{A}_{i}\to\mathbf{Lax}_{s}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
. By the preceding part, this is equally to say that the corresponding tight binary maps
F^{a_{1}}
and
F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}
are sharp. It remains, therefore, to show that the condition that
F_{b}
is sharp is redundant. Indeed, since
F
is tight, so is
F_{b}
, so we must only show that
(F_{b})^{a_{1}}
and
(F_{b})_{a_{2}}
are strict, but these equal
(F^{a_{1}})_{b}
and
(F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}})_{b}
which are strict since
F^{a_{1}}
and
F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}
are sharp.

For
n=3
, consider a tight ternary map
\overline{F}\colon\mathcal{A}_{1},\mathcal{A}_{2},\mathcal{A}_{3}\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
with associated tight
4
-ary map
F\colon\mathcal{A}_{1},\mathcal{A}_{2},\mathcal{A}_{3},\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}
. Arguing as before, to say that
\overline{F}
factors through
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})_{s}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C})
via a sharp ternary map is just to say that each of the ternary maps
F^{a_{1}}
,
F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}
and
F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{3}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{3}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{3}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{3}$}}}
are sharp. Therefore it suffices to show the condition that
F_{b}
is sharp is redundant. Since
F_{b}
is tight, this follows from the fact that
(F_{b})^{a_{1}}=(F^{a_{1}})_{b}
,
(F_{b})\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}=(F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{2}$}}})_{b}
and
(F_{b})_{a_{3}}=(F\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{3}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptstyle a_{3}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{3}$}}}{\vbox{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a_{3}$}}})_{b}
and each of these are sharp.

∎

7.1.
The associated skew monoidal closed structure

As usual, combining Theorem
7.5
with Section
2.6
, we obtain:

Theorem 7.6
.

There are closed skew monoidal structures
(\mathbf{G}\text{-}\mathbf{Cat},\otimes^{\sharp}_{l},\mathbf{1})
and
(\mathbf{G}\text{-}\mathbf{Cat},\otimes^{\sharp}_{p},\mathbf{1})
, having internal homs
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})_{s}
and
\mathbf{Psd}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})_{s}
.

•

The tensor products
\mathcal{A}\otimes^{\sharp}_{l}\mathcal{B}
and
\mathcal{A}\otimes^{\sharp}_{p}\mathcal{B}
classify sharp lax binary maps and sharp pseudo binary maps, respectively. Both admit presentations, obtained by modifying the presentations in Section
5.3
and Section
6.4
for
\mathcal{A}\otimes_{l}\mathcal{B}
and
\mathcal{A}\otimes_{p}\mathcal{B}
respectively simply by adding the equation asserting that
T^{a}_{B_{2},B_{1}}
is an identity 2-cell.

•

Both skew monoidal structures are right normal as before but now they are also left normal. Indeed,
\mathbf{1}\otimes^{\sharp}_{l}\mathcal{A}
classifies loose unary maps in
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}
but, in this restricted setting, these are just the strict maps, and so classified by
\mathcal{A}
itself. The associator for neither skew monoidal closed structure is invertible — for instance,
(\mathbf{2}\otimes^{\sharp}_{l}\mathbf{2})\otimes^{\sharp}_{l}\mathbf{2}
and
\mathbf{2}\otimes^{\sharp}_{l}(\mathbf{2}\otimes^{\sharp}_{l}\mathbf{2})
are not isomorphic.

•

Both skew monoidal closed structures give rise to skew closed structures in the sense of Street
[
37
]
— in fact, since these skew monoidal structures are left and right normal, the corresponding skew closed structures are in fact closed categories in the sense of Eilenberg and Kelly
[
16
]
.

•

In a followup paper, we will show that the skew structure
(\mathbf{G}\text{-}\mathbf{Cat},\otimes^{\sharp}_{p},\mathbf{1})
is homotopically well behaved with respect to Lack’s model structure on
\mathbf{G}\text{-}\mathbf{Cat}

[
30
]
. Furthermore, we will show that it descends to a symmetric monoidal closed structure on the homotopy category of Gray-categories. This implies, for instance, that the associators
(\mathcal{A}\otimes^{\sharp}_{p}\mathcal{B})\otimes^{\sharp}_{p}\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{A}\otimes^{\sharp}_{p}(\mathcal{B}\otimes^{\sharp}_{p}\mathcal{C})
are triequivalences whenever
\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}
and
\mathcal{C}
are cofibrant Gray-categories.

The reader is entitled to wonder whether we could give a simplified construction of the
4
-ary multicategories of sharp multimaps, without considering pseudomaps and the larger skew multicategories
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}
and
\mathbb{P}\mathbf{sd}
at all. It is not clear that this is the case.

The reason is that if
F\colon\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}
and
G\colon\mathcal{X},\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
are sharp lax binary maps, our construction of
G\circ_{2}F
will still pass through pseudomaps. Indeed, our construction used the dual
d_{2}G\colon\mathcal{C}^{co},\mathcal{X}^{co}\to\mathcal{D}^{co}
but this need not be tight, so that the adjoint map
\mathcal{C}^{co}\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{X}^{co},\mathcal{D}^{co})
is only a pseudomap. Since the definition of
G\circ_{2}F
ultimately uses this, pseudomaps cannot be easily eliminated!

A closely related issue is that since a sharp map
\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}
only induces a pseudomap
\mathcal{B}\to\mathbf{Oplax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{C})
, the multicategory
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}
is not biclosed. One only obtains biclosedness in the larger
4
-ary multicategory
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{l}
of loose multimaps. But this suffers from not being left representable. In between
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}
and
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{l}
, we have the
4
-ary skew multicategory
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}
which, in addition to being left representable and closed, contains both
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{\sharp}
and
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}^{l}
as canonically associated
4
-ary multicategories.

Appendix A
Axioms for
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})

A.1.
Pseudomaps

A pseudomap

(i)

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(\psi:\phi)}

=

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Ff_{2}Ff^{\prime}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Ff^{\prime}_{2}Ff^{\prime}_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Ff^{\prime}_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(f_{2}f_{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(f^{\prime}_{2}f^{\prime}_{1}).}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(f^{\prime}_{2}f_{1})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(\psi\circ 1)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(1\circ\phi)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\psi\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{2}_{f^{\prime}_{2},f^{\prime}_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\psi\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\psi:F\phi}

where the unlabelled regions commute by (
v
).

(viii)

Compatibility of
F^{2}
with the interchange map:

at 1-cells
f_{1}\colon x\to y
,
f_{2}\colon y\to z
,
f_{3}\colon z\to w
and
f_{4}\colon w\to u
in
\mathcal{A}
we have the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Fy}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Fw}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Fx}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Fz}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Fu.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ff_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ff_{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ff_{3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ff_{4}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(f_{2}f_{1})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(f_{4}f_{3})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{2}_{f_{4},f_{3}}}

and require the equality of
3
-cells
F^{2}_{f_{4},f_{3}}:F^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}=1
, remarking that the lhs is automatically an endo-
3
-cell by (
iii
).

Compatibility of

with 2-cells and the interchange:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces z}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces w,}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{1}}

we require the equations

and

,
remarking again that both

-cells on the lhs of equations are endomorphisms by three instances of (

) and two of (

).

A.2.
Lax Transformations

A lax transformation
\alpha\colon F\to G
has to satisfy the following axioms.

(i)

Degeneracy for the 2-cell component:

at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
, then
\alpha_{1_{x}}=1_{\alpha_{x}}
.

(ii)

Compatibility with 3-cells:

at
1
-cells
f,f^{\prime}\colon x\to y
,
2
-cells
\phi,\phi^{\prime}\colon f\to f^{\prime}
and a
3
-cell
\Gamma\colon\phi\to\phi^{\prime}
, we require:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{=}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf^{\prime}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf^{\prime}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff^{\prime}.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\phi^{\prime}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\phi^{\prime}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\phi\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\Gamma}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{\phi^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{\phi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\Gamma\circ 1}

(iii)

Compatibility with vertical composition of 2-cells:

at
1
-cells
f,f^{\prime},f^{\prime\prime}\colon x\to y
and
2
-cells
\phi_{1}\colon f\to f^{\prime},\phi_{2}\colon f^{\prime}\to f^{\prime\prime}
in
\mathcal{A}
, we require:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf^{\prime}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{=}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf^{\prime\prime}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff^{\prime\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf^{\prime\prime}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff^{\prime\prime}.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\phi_{2}\cdot\phi_{1})\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F(\phi_{2}\cdot\phi_{1})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f^{\prime\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f^{\prime\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi_{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi_{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\phi_{1}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\phi_{2}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{\phi_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{\phi_{2}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{\phi_{2}\cdot\phi_{1}}}

(iv)

Degeneracy for the 3-cell component:
at a
1
-cell
f\colon x\to y
we require
\alpha_{1_{f}}=1_{\alpha_{f}}
.

(v)

Compatibility with composition of 1-cells:
at composable
1
-cells

,
f_{2}\colon x\to y
and
f_{3}\colon y\to z
in
\mathcal{A}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{3}Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{w}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{3}\alpha_{y}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}Ff_{3}F(f_{2}f_{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{3}f_{2}f_{1})\alpha_{w}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}F(f_{3}f_{2}f_{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{=}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{3}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{3}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{3}f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}f_{1}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{3}Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{w}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{3}Gf_{2}\alpha_{x}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{3}\alpha_{y}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}Ff_{3}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{3}f_{2})Gf_{1}\alpha_{w}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{3}f_{2})\alpha_{x}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}F(f_{3}f_{2})Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{3}f_{2}f_{1})\alpha_{w}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}F(f_{3}f_{2}f_{1}).}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{3}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{3}f_{2},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{3}f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{3}f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{3}f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{2}_{f_{3},f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{2}_{f_{3}f_{2},f_{1}}}

(vi)

Degeneracy for

-cell

, we require

(vii)

(L)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{x}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{2}}\circ 1}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{2}}\circ 1}

noting that the vertical paths in the two diagrams are equal by (

) for

and

.

Similarly, given a diagram in

we require:

(R)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{X}}}

A.3.
Modifications

A modification
\Gamma\colon\alpha\to\beta
has to satisfy the following axioms.

(i)

Degeneracy for the 3-cell component:
at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
,
\Gamma_{1_{x}}=1_{\Gamma_{x}}
.

(ii)

Compatibility with composition of 1-cells:

at
1
-cells
f_{1}\colon x\to y
and
f_{2}\colon y\to z
in
\mathcal{A}
,

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\beta_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}\alpha_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}\beta_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{2}f_{1})\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{1,1,1}Gf_{2}\alpha_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}F(f_{2}f_{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}F(f_{2}f_{1})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{z}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{2}^{\prime},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Gamma_{x}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\beta_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Gamma_{y}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{2}^{\prime},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{2}^{\prime},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{z}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Gamma_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{f_{2}}\circ 1}

=

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{1,1,1}Gf_{2}\beta_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\beta_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf_{2}\beta_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{2}f_{1})\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(f_{2}f_{1})\beta_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{1,1,1}Gf_{2}\beta_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{z}F(f_{2}f_{1})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}F(f_{2}f_{1}).}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{2}^{\prime},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Gamma_{x}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\beta_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{2}^{\prime},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{z}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{f_{2}^{\prime},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Gamma_{x}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma_{f_{2}f_{1}}}

(iii)

Compatibility with 2-cells:

at
1
-cells
f,f^{\prime}\colon x\to y
and a
2
-cell
\phi\colon f\to f^{\prime}
, we require:

Appendix B
The Gray-categorical structure of
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})

Let
\mathcal{A}
and
\mathcal{B}
be Gray-categories. We now describe the operations equipping
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
with the structure of a Gray-category.

B.1.
The category of pseudo-functors and lax transformations

Given a pseudomap
F\colon\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}
, the identity lax transformation
1_{F}\colon F\to F\in\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
is given by the identity in each component.

Let
\alpha\colon F\to G
and
\beta\colon G\to H
be lax transformations. The lax transformation
\beta\cdot\alpha\colon F\to H
is defined as follows:

•

at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
,
(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{x}:=\beta_{x}\alpha_{x}\colon Fx\to Gx\to Hx
;

•

at a 1-cell
f\colon x\to y
in
\mathcal{A}
, the 2-cell
(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{f}\colon Hf(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{x}\to(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{y}Ff
is the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Hf(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{x}=Hf\beta_{x}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}\alpha_{y}Ff=(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{y}Ff;}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f}}

•

at a 2-cell
\phi\colon f\to f^{\prime}
,
(\beta\cdot\alpha)_{\phi}
is the composite

(17)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Hf\beta_{x}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}\alpha_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Hf^{\prime}\beta_{x}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}Gf^{\prime}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}\alpha_{y}Ff^{\prime};}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H\phi\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G\phi\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f^{\prime}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{\phi}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{\phi}}

•

at 1-cells
f_{1}\colon x\to y
and
f_{2}\colon y\to z
in
\mathcal{A}
, the invertible 3-cell
(\beta\cdot\alpha)^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}
is the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Hf_{2}Hf_{1}\beta_{x}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Hf_{2}\beta_{y}Gf_{1}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Hf_{2}\beta_{y}\alpha_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}Gf_{2}\alpha_{y}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}\alpha_{z}Ff_{2}Ff_{1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}Gf_{2}Gf_{1}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{H(f_{2}f_{1})\beta_{x}\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}G(f_{2}f_{1})\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{z}\alpha_{z}F(f_{2}f_{1}).}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\beta_{f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f_{2}f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{2}f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f_{2}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha_{f_{1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\alpha^{2}_{f_{2},f_{1}}}

B.2.
Hom-2-categories
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})[F,G]

B.2.1.
Composition of modifications

Given a lax transformation
\alpha\colon F\to G\in\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
, the identity modification
1_{\alpha}\colon\alpha\to\alpha
is given by the identity in each component.

Let
\alpha,\beta,\gamma\colon F\to G
be lax transformations and
\Lambda\colon\alpha\to\beta
and
\Lambda^{\prime}\colon\beta\to\gamma
be modifications. Then the modification
\Lambda^{\prime}\ast\Lambda\colon\alpha\to\gamma
is defined by:

•

at

,
(\Lambda^{\prime}\ast\Lambda)_{x}:=\Lambda^{\prime}_{x}\cdot\Lambda_{x}\colon\alpha_{x}\to\beta_{x}\to\gamma_{x}
;

•

at
f\colon x\to y\in\mathcal{A}
,
(\Lambda^{\prime}\ast\Lambda)_{f}
is the composite

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\beta_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{Gf\gamma_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\alpha_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{y}Ff}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\gamma_{y}Ff.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda_{y}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda^{\prime}_{y}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Lambda_{x}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\Lambda^{\prime}_{x}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda^{\prime}_{f}}

B.2.2.
Composition of perturbations

Given a modification
\Lambda\colon\alpha\to\beta\in\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})[F,G]
, the identity perturbation
1_{\Lambda}\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda
has
(1_{\Lambda})_{x}:=1_{\Lambda_{x}}
at
x\in\mathcal{A}
.

Let
\theta\colon\Lambda\to\Gamma
and
\theta^{\prime}\colon\Gamma\to\Omega
be composable perturbations in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
. The perturbation
\theta^{\prime}\theta\colon\Lambda\to\Omega
has component, at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
, the 3-cell

(\theta^{\prime}\theta)_{x}:=\theta^{\prime}_{x}\ast\theta_{x}\colon\Lambda_{x}\to\Gamma_{x}\to\Omega_{x}.

Appendix C
The action of
\mathbf{Lax}(-,-)
on pseudomaps

In this section, given pseudomaps
F\colon\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
and
G\colon\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{B}^{\prime}
, we will spell out the action of the strict map
\mathbf{Lax}(F,\mathcal{B})\colon\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime},\mathcal{B})\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
and the pseudomap
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)\colon\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}^{\prime})
. These two maps are defined using left and right whiskering respectively.

C.1.
The strict map
\mathbf{Lax}(F,\mathcal{B})

For any pseudomap
F\colon\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
,
\mathbf{Lax}(F,\mathcal{B})
is a strict map, so it is specified by its action on pseudomaps, lax transformations, modifications and perturbations. At a pseudomap
G\colon\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\to\mathcal{B}
, we have
\mathbf{Lax}(F,\mathcal{B})G=GF
.

C.1.1.
Left whiskering of lax transformations

Given the following diagram in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{A}^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta}

the lax transformation
\mathbf{Lax}(F,\mathcal{B})(\beta)=\beta F\colon GF\to G^{\prime}F
is defined by:

•

at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
,
(\beta F)_{x}:=\beta_{Fx}\colon GFx\to G^{\prime}Fx
;

•

at a 1-cell

in
\mathcal{A}
,

;

•

at a 2-cell

in
\mathcal{A}
,

is defined as

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{\prime}Ff\beta_{Fx}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{Fy}GFf}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{\prime}Ff^{\prime}\beta_{Fx}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{Fy}GFf^{\prime};}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{Ff}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{Ff^{\prime}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ GF\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{F\phi}}

•

at composable 1-cells

and

in
\mathcal{A}
, the invertible 3-cell

in
\mathcal{B}
is defined as

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{\prime}FgG^{\prime}Ff\beta_{Fx}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{\prime}Fg\beta_{Fy}GFf}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{Fz}GFgGFf}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{\prime}(FgFf)\beta_{Fx}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{Fz}G(FgFf)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF(gf)\beta_{Fx}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\beta_{Fz}GF(gf),}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ\beta_{Ff}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{Fg}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{F(gf)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{\prime}}^{2}_{Fg,Ff}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G({F}^{2}_{g,f})\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G^{2}_{Fg,Ff}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G(F^{2}_{g,f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{FgFf}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta_{F^{2}_{g,f}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta^{2}_{Fg,Ff}}

where the 3-cell

is invertible because

is an invertible 2-cell (this follows from Axiom (

) of a lax transformation).

C.1.3.
Left whiskering of perturbations

Let
\delta\colon\Theta\to\Lambda
be a perturbation in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime},\mathcal{B})
. The perturbation
\mathbf{Lax}(F,\mathcal{B})(\delta)=\delta F\colon\Theta F\to\Lambda F
is defined, at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
, as
(\delta F)_{x}:=\delta_{Fx}\colon\Theta_{Fx}\to\Lambda_{Fx}
.

C.2.
The pseudomap
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)

To describe the pseudomap
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)\colon\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})\to\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}^{\prime})
, we must specify its action on pseudomaps, lax transformations, modifications, perturbations and also describe the cocycles
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)^{2}
. At a pseudomap
F\colon\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}
, it is defined by
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)(F)=GF
.

C.2.1.
Right whiskering of lax transformations

Given the following diagram in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}^{\prime})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{B}^{\prime},}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}

the lax transformation
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)(\alpha)=G\alpha\colon GF\to GF^{\prime}
is defined by:

•

at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
,
(G\alpha)_{x}:=G(\alpha_{x})\colon GFx\to GF^{\prime}x
.

•

at a 1-cell
f\colon x\to y
in
\mathcal{A}
,
(G\alpha)_{f}
is defined as

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}f\circ G\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}f\circ\alpha_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha_{y}\circ Ff)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha_{y}\circ GFf.}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{F^{\prime}f,\alpha_{x}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha_{f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}_{\alpha_{y},Ff}}^{-1}}

Note that this composite is just
G(\alpha_{f})
if
G
is a Gray-functor.

•

at a 2-cell
\phi\colon f\to f^{\prime}
in
\mathcal{A}
,
(G\alpha)_{\phi}
is defined as the 3-cell

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}f\circ G\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}f\circ\alpha_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha_{y}\circ Ff)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha_{y}\circ GFf}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}f^{\prime}\circ G\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}f^{\prime}\circ\alpha_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha_{y}\circ Ff^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha_{y}\circ GFf^{\prime},}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}_{\alpha_{y},Ff}}^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha_{f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{F^{\prime}f,\alpha_{x}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ GF\phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(1\circ F\phi)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}_{\alpha_{y},Ff^{\prime}}}^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(F^{\prime}\phi\circ 1)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces GF^{\prime}\phi\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha_{f^{\prime}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}_{F^{\prime}f^{\prime},\alpha_{x}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha_{\phi})}

where the left and right square commute by Axiom (
v
) for
GF
and
GF^{\prime}
as pseudomaps;

•

at composable 1-cells
f\colon x\to y
and
g\colon y\to z
in
\mathcal{A}
, the invertible 3-cell
(G\alpha)^{2}_{g,f}
in
\mathcal{B}^{\prime}
is defined as

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}gGF^{\prime}fG\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}gF^{\prime}f)G\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}gF^{\prime}f\alpha_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}g\alpha_{y}Ff)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha_{z}FgFf)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha_{z}G(FgFf)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}(gf)G\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}(gf)\alpha_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha_{z}F(gf))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha_{z}GF(gf).}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha_{gf})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G({F^{\prime}}^{2}_{g,f})\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}}_{F^{\prime}(gf),\alpha_{x}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}}^{-1}_{\alpha_{z},F(gf)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G({F}^{2}_{g,f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}_{F^{\prime}g,F^{\prime}f}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G({F^{\prime}}^{2}_{g,f}\circ 1)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(1\circ{F}^{2}_{g,f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(1\circ\alpha_{f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha_{g}\circ 1)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}}^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\alpha^{2}_{g,f})}

C.2.2.
Right whiskering of modifications

Let
\Lambda\colon\alpha\to\alpha^{\prime}
be a modification in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
. The modification
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)(\Lambda)=G\Lambda\colon G\alpha\to G\alpha^{\prime}
is given by:

•

at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
the 2-cell
(G\Lambda)_{x}:=G\Lambda_{x}\colon G\alpha_{x}\to G\alpha_{x}
in
\mathcal{B}^{\prime}
.

•

at a 1-cell
f\colon x\to y
in
\mathcal{A}
the 3-cell
(G\Lambda)_{f}
in
\mathcal{B}^{\prime}
is defined as

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}fG\alpha_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{GF^{\prime}fG\alpha^{\prime}_{x}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}f\alpha_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(F^{\prime}f\alpha^{\prime}_{x})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha_{y}Ff)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G(\alpha^{\prime}_{y}Ff)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha_{y}GFf}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G\alpha^{\prime}_{y}GFf,}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ G\Lambda_{x}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\Lambda_{y}\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\alpha^{\prime}_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\alpha_{f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(1\circ\Lambda_{x})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\Lambda_{y}\circ 1)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G^{2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}}^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{G^{2}}^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\Lambda_{f})}

where the top and bottom squares commute by Axiom (
v
) for
G
.

C.2.3.
Right whiskering of perturbations

Let
\theta\colon\Delta\to\Gamma
be a perturbation in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
. The perturbation
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)(\theta)=G\theta\colon G\Delta\to G\Gamma
is defined, at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
, as
(G\theta)_{x}:=G\theta_{x}\colon G\Delta_{x}\to G\Gamma_{x}
.

C.2.4.
Cocycle for
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)

At composable 1-cells
\alpha\colon F\to F^{\prime}
and
\alpha^{\prime}\colon F^{\prime}\to F^{\prime\prime}
in
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})
, the cocyle invertible modification
\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)^{2}_{\alpha^{\prime},\alpha}\colon G\alpha^{\prime}\cdot G\alpha\to G(\alpha^{\prime}\cdot\alpha)
is defined by:

•

at an object
x\in\mathcal{A}
,
(\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)^{2}_{\alpha^{\prime},\alpha})_{x}
is the invertible 2-cell

G^{2}_{\alpha^{\prime}_{x},\alpha_{x}}\colon G\alpha^{\prime}_{x}\circ G\alpha_{x}\to G(\alpha^{\prime}_{x}\circ\alpha_{x});

•

at a 1-cell
f\colon x\to y\in\mathcal{A}
,
(\mathbf{Lax}(\mathcal{A},G)^{2}_{\alpha^{\prime},\alpha})_{f}
is the identity.

Appendix D
Axioms for multimaps in
\mathbb{L}\mathbf{ax}

D.1.
Axioms for binary maps

Compatibility of
A_{\beta}
with 3-cells
\Theta\colon\beta\rightarrow\beta^{\prime}
in
\mathcal{B}
,

(
A:\Theta
)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B)F_{b}(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A)F^{a}(B)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B^{\prime})F_{b}(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A)F^{a}(B^{\prime})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{a^{\prime}}(\beta)\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{B^{\prime}}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{a^{\prime}}(\beta^{\prime})\circ 1}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{\beta}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B)F_{b}(A)}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A)F^{a}(B^{\prime})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{a}(\beta)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{a^{\prime}}(\beta^{\prime})\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{a}(\beta^{\prime})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{B^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F^{a^{\prime}}(\Theta)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{\beta^{\prime}}}

and
of
\alpha_{B}
with 3-cells

in
\mathcal{A}
,

(

)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B)F_{b}(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B)F_{b}(A^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B)F_{b}(A)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F^{a^{\prime}}(B)F_{b}(A^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A)F^{a}(B)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A^{\prime})F^{a}(B)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A)F^{a}(B)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F_{b^{\prime}}(A^{\prime})F^{a}(B).}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F_{b}(\alpha)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{b^{\prime}}(\alpha)\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A^{\prime}_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{b^{\prime}}(\alpha^{\prime})\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F_{b}(\alpha)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{b^{\prime}}(\alpha^{\prime})\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F_{b}(\alpha^{\prime})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A^{\prime}_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{b^{\prime}}(\Lambda)\circ 1}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha^{\prime}_{B}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1\circ F_{b}(\Lambda)}

Degeneracy equations:

(D-
A_{1},A_{2}:b
)

F_{b}^{1_{a^{\prime}},A}=F_{b}^{A,1_{a}}=1_{F^{A}_{b}}

(D-
1_{a}:B
)

(1_{a})_{B}=1_{F^{a}_{B}}

(D-
1_{A}:B
)

(1_{A})_{B}=1_{A_{B}}

(D-
1_{a}:\beta
)

(1_{a})_{\beta}=1_{F^{a}_{\beta}}

(D-
A_{1},A_{2}:B
)

F_{B}^{1_{a^{\prime}},A}=F_{B}^{A,1_{a}}=1_{A_{B}}

(D-
A_{1},A_{2}:1_{b}
)

F_{1_{b}}^{A_{2},A_{1}}=1_{F_{b}^{A_{2},A_{1}}}

(D-
a:B_{1},B_{2}
)

F^{a}_{1_{b^{\prime}},B}=F^{a}_{B,1_{b}}=1_{F^{a}_{B}}

(D-
A:1_{b}
)

A_{1_{b}}=1_{F^{A}_{b}}

(D-
\alpha:1_{b}
)

\alpha_{1_{b}}=1_{F^{\alpha}_{b}}

(D-
A:1_{B}
)

A_{1_{B}}=1_{A_{B}}

(D-
A:B_{1},B_{2}
)

F^{A}_{1_{b^{\prime}},B}=F^{A}_{B,1_{b}}=1_{A_{B}}

(D-
1_{a}:B_{1},B_{2}
)

F^{1_{a}}_{B_{2},B_{1}}=1_{F^{a}_{B_{2},B_{1}}}

D.2.
Axioms for ternary maps

Compatibility of

Degeneracy equations:

(
1_{a}:B:C
)

(1_{a}\mid B\mid C)=1_{{B_{C}}^{a}}

(
A:1_{b}:C
)

(A\mid 1_{b}\mid C)=1_{{A_{C}}^{b}}

(
A:B:1_{c}
)

(A\mid B\mid 1_{c})=1_{{A_{B}}^{c}}

D.3.
Axiom for 4-ary maps

There is a single axiom for
4
-ary maps, which we call the
mecon axiom
, since its shape is a truncated octahedron, also known as a mecon. Each of the nodes of the diagram consists of a composite of four
1
-cells, and we encode these using sequences of
A,B,C
and
D
, which uniquely encode the composite as follows. Firstly, let us write
F(a,-,-,-)
for the ternary map which we usually call
F^{a}
and so on; then,
F(a,b,-,d)
represents the associated pseudomap. Each appearance of
C
on a node represents a
1
-cell of the form
F(x,y,C,z)
where
x\in\{a,a^{\prime}\}
,
y\in\{b,b^{\prime}\}
,
z\in\{d,d^{\prime}\}
. and similarly for
A,B
and
D
. The only question is which of the two values we choose for each of
x,y
and
z
. This is determined by the ordering. For instance, consider
DBAC
. Since
C
appears at the end, before
D,B,A
, none of
d,b
nor
a
are primed — thus
C
is replaced by
F(a,b,C,d)
; as
A
appears after
C
, but before
D
and
B
, we prime
c
but neither
d
nor
b
— thus
A
is replaced by
F(A,b,c^{\prime},d)
. Continuing in this way, priming lowercase letters that appear before the uppercase letter in question, we see that
DBAC
encodes the composite
1
-cell
F(a^{\prime},b^{\prime},c^{\prime},D)F(a^{\prime},B,c^{\prime},d)F(A,b,c^{\prime},D)F(a,b,C,d)
.

(Mcn)
